memory_candidates.content: In this agent system's deploy pipeline (verify-deploy.sh), gates come in two invocation flavors distinguished by which tree they audit: gates 6/7/11/12 invoke the SOURCE-STORE copy of their lint script with a REPO_ROOT="$TARGET" override (correct for a lint whose default scan corpus is agent-system/extensions/** paths), while gate 9 (lint-postflight-boundary.sh) deliberately invokes the DEPLOYED .claude/ copy instead, because that script's own PROJECT_ROOT resolution (3-levels-up from scripts/lint/) only lands on the repo root from the deployed path depth, and its default scan targets are .claude/skills and .claude/extensions. When adding a new lint gate, check which convention your script's own root-resolution and default scan-glob assume before choosing how to wire it into verify-deploy.sh -- picking the wrong one silently scans nothing.

test-skill-base-lifecycle.sh (and similarly-structured lint/function test suites in this repo) resolve their target script via a deployed-tree-first, source-store-fallback candidate list, matching real SKILL.md runtime assumptions. This means such a suite can show a false pre-deploy failure for a source-store-only fix even though the fix's logic is already correct -- verify by sourcing/invoking the source-store copy directly as an interim check, and re-run the official suite after deploy-headless.sh to get the true, fully-green result. Don't mistake this deploy-staleness artifact for a logic defect in the new code.

When editing a context/patterns or project doc file tracked in an extension's index-entries.json, always check for and update that file's own declared line_count entry in the same commit -- check-extension-docs.sh's Rule R fails on any drift, and it is easy to grow or shrink a doc file during an unrelated content fix (e.g. rewriting a stale section) without noticing the index entry needs a matching update. This surfaced as a real, self-introduced regression during this task's own pre-deploy verify-deploy.sh baseline capture.
